narrative: Markets are grappling with a volatile mix of hawkish central bank policy, escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, and restrictive US tech export controls. While Nvidia's strong earnings and guidance provided a temporary reprieve, the broader tech sector remains under pressure from regulatory headwinds and rising Treasury yields. Investors are increasingly concerned about sticky inflation and the potential for further Fed rate hikes, leading to a rotation out of crowded risk positions. Geopolitical instability, particularly regarding US-Iran tensions, continues to introduce uncertainty into energy markets. The upcoming Anthropic IPO serves as a critical test for investor appetite in the AI space amidst this tightening environment.

Nasdaq.why: Nvidia's strong earnings provide a positive catalyst, but the index faces significant headwinds from US export restrictions on AI chips and concerns over regulatory impacts on tech talent.

S&P 500.why: The index has suffered consecutive declines as investors rotate out of risk, pressured by restrictive Fed commentary and broader tech sector weakness.

Gold.why: Gold is under significant pressure, currently on track for its worst annual performance since 2013.

Oil.why: Prices are caught between bullish geopolitical risk premiums from Middle East tensions and bearish concerns regarding potential supply gluts.

priced_in: Higher interest rates for a longer duration
Approximately three 25 bps Fed rate hikes over the next six months
Regulatory headwinds for tech firms due to export controls and immigration rules
debates: Whether AI productivity gains will be sufficient to offset persistent inflationary pressures
The sustainability of tech valuations given the potential for slowing gross margins and export restrictions
watch_next: US retail sales and industrial production data
Microsoft Ignite speech by Satya Nadella
